subtype: Following with the eyes and joint attention [Expressing]
passage:
“Kishore, where's Papa?” asked Ujjwal, walking across the room. Kishore's eyes followed him step by step.
“Look, Kishore. Kite!” Ujjwal pointed out of the window at a red kite over the rooftops.
Kishore turned his head to the window, then back at his father's face. “Kite,” he said, pointing too.
“Yes, kite! You saw it.”
Kishore kept watching until the red shape slid behind the water tank.

qa.q: What did Ujjwal point at through the window?
qa.a: A red kite over the rooftops.

qa.q: What does Kishore's glance back at his father seem to show?
qa.a: It seems to show he was interested and wanted to share the sight with Ujjwal. It could also be that he was checking whether the word Ujjwal used was the right one.

qa.q: What could Ujjwal do next to keep the shared looking going?
qa.a: He could point at other things, say their names, and pause to see whether Kishore looks where he points.

qa.q: How might Ujjwal feel when Kishore follows his point?
qa.a: He is likely to feel delighted and connected, because his son is looking with him and not just at him. 🙂

grounding: A toddler tracks a parent with his eyes and follows a point to share attention on an object.

subtype: Following with the eyes and joint attention [Expressing]
passage: Playgroup note, Friday. Ayesha, almost two, watched me across the room while I set out cups, turning her head as I moved. When I pointed to the picture of a cat on the wall and said “Look, a cat,” she looked at the cat, then at me, and pointed too. She stayed with the picture for a long moment. I said “cat” again and waved at it. I will tell her mother how well she looks along with us. 🙂 Kavitha

qa.q: Who wrote the note, and what did Ayesha look at after the pointing?
qa.a: Kavitha wrote it, and Ayesha looked at the picture of a cat on the wall.

qa.q: What does Ayesha's look from the cat to Kavitha suggest she was thinking?
qa.a: It suggests she was interested and wanted to share the cat with Kavitha, since she pointed as well. It could also mean she was checking Kavitha's reaction.

qa.q: What might Kavitha say to Ayesha's mother?
qa.a: Kavitha might describe what they saw, that Ayesha follows a pointing finger and shares her attention, and if the mother has any questions about her child's development she can ask a paediatrician.

qa.q: How might Ayesha see Kavitha's naming of the cat?
qa.a: She may feel that her attention is noticed and welcomed, and that a shared look comes with a word attached, which helps her learn.

grounding: A toddler follows a caregiver with her eyes and looks where the adult points, sharing attention on an object.
